cohort: All pregnant women treated for ruptured uterus at a single center in Shanghai, China between 2013 and 2020 (N=41)
finding: The incidence of uterine rupture was 1.96/10,000 births, and while there were no maternal deaths, perinatal fatality related to uterine rupture was 7.3%, with cases involving a history of laparoscopic myomectomy being more likely to have serious adverse outcomes.
mod_finding: Previous cesarean section was the most common cause of uterine rupture, while cases with a history of laparoscopic myomectomy were more likely to have serious adverse outcomes, such as fetal death.
